title: Base Read/Write Multiple Registers variant 5
purpose: Use a write-register setup followed by a distinct read/write-multiple-registers request to exercise stateful sequencing and both write and combined access paths.
expected_behavior: The first request may write two registers at address 0030. The second may read two registers at 0010 and write two registers at 0020 with values 1111 and 2222; a server may instead return standard exceptions for unsupported or inaccessible addresses.
constraints_preserved: Both messages use 7-byte MBAP headers and protocol identifier 0000.
First MBAP length 000b matches unit plus the 10-byte function-16 PDU.
Function-16 quantity 0002 and byte count 04 match the two 16-bit values.
Second MBAP length 000f matches unit plus the 14-byte function-17 PDU.
Function-17 read and write quantities are both 0002, and write byte count 04 matches the two values.
Transaction identifiers differ and message order is preserved.
Unit identifier 01 is consistent across the sequence.
issue_safety_notes: No external vulnerability or issue knowledge is available. Modbus/TCP commonly does not require application state between these operations, so the setup relationship is an intentional sequence-coverage heuristic rather than a claimed protocol requirement.
